$comment: Neutral shipped <unistd.h> (POSIX) — c14 (linux) + c15c (macOS). The core POSIX I/O syscalls SQLite's os_unix.c routes through its aSyscall table. The LP64 widths (ssize_t/off_t=i64, size_t=u64) AGREE between Linux and macOS, and SEEK_* + the access() mode bits F_OK/R_OK/W_OK/X_OK are byte-identical (verified against xnu/bsd/sys/unistd.h + _seek_set.h) — so every constant + signature stays flat (no per-format variant). fdatasync + fallocate are LINUX-ONLY (macOS uses fcntl F_FULLFSYNC / F_PREALLOCATE): each carries a per-symbol `availableObjectFormats` of elf-only so it is NOT injected on a macho target (DSS imports EVERY declared shipped extern → a macho-declared fdatasync would plant an undefined import; libSystem has no fdatasync). They ARE injected on elf for linux SQLite's use. (D-SHIPPED-SYMBOL-PER-TARGET-AVAILABILITY) Gated availableObjectFormats:[elf,macho] (elf=WSL run target, macho=macos-latest leg). No over-ship: SQLite's aSyscall surface. open/fcntl/fstat/lstat/stat/mkdir/mmap live in their own headers. c53 += lseek/sysconf/getpid (elf+macho) for os_unix seek/page-size/pid + the _SC_PAGESIZE constant. lseek returns off_t=i64 (NOT i32 — SQLite assigns the result to an i64; a 32-bit return would sign-truncate >2GB file offsets) and ships as PLAIN `lseek` not lseek64 (the default model leaves __USE_FILE_OFFSET64 off, so libc exports the plain name with off_t=8; verified by nm of an -O0 compile). _SC_PAGESIZE DIVERGES per-format (elf=30 / macho=29) so it ships with per-target `variants` (the FILENAME_MAX mechanism); both linux arches share 30 (glibc bits/confname.h is arch-generic). â c82 (shell.c CLI): symlink(target,linkpath), isatty(fd), getuid() [uid_t=u32 LP64, the geteuid twin], sleep(seconds)->unslept, usleep(useconds_t=u32) â glibc /usr/include/unistd.h prototypes, identical on Darwin (ride the header [elf,macho] gate). shell.c self-declares `extern int isatty(int);` at file scope â goal-2 lets the user decl win harmlessly (same signature); the descriptor entry serves every other consumer. ★ c85 (shell.c `.cd` command): chdir(path) — glibc prototype verified /usr/include/unistd.h `extern int chdir (const char *__path)`, exported W chdir@GLIBC both arches (nm -D libc.so.6 x86_64+aarch64); identical on Darwin per POSIX (rides the header [elf,macho] gate — the getcwd sibling). C34a (2026-07-21, D-FFI-TCL-DESCRIPTOR test1.c bundle): += _SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN for sqlite src/test1.c:32732 `sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)`. glibc bits/confname.h enumerates _SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN = 84 (elf, both arches — arch-generic like _SC_PAGESIZE). Darwin's value DIVERGES (58) and is not yet witnessed, so this ships as an ELF-ONLY `variants` arm (the _SC_PAGESIZE per-format precedent): a macho target selects no variant -> not injected -> a macho reference fails LOUD rather than folding a guessed value (the fail-loud-over-guess law). TF-C68 (D-FFI-OS-UNIX-LFS-ISNAN-SYMBOLS): += pread64/pwrite64 — the glibc `_LARGEFILE64_SOURCE` 64-bit-offset variants os_unix.c address-takes into aSyscall[] under USE_PREAD64 (Linux-only; macOS/Windows never define it). Signature = plain pread/pwrite (the LP64 off_t is already i64, so off64_t here is i64 too). ELF-ONLY (`availableObjectFormats:[elf]`, the fdatasync/fallocate precedent): macho's libSystem has no pread64, and DSS eager-imports every declared shipped extern, so a macho-declared pread64 would plant an undefined import. glibc exports both WEAK (nm -D libc.so.6: `W pread64@@GLIBC_2.2.5`) — weak = eager-import-safe. ★ D-CSUBSET-DARWIN-BSD-SYMBOL-CLUSTER: fsctl + uuid_t — the Darwin-extensions region of the SDK unistd.h, reached by os_unix.c's plain `#include <unistd.h>` (os_unix.c:94) which THIS descriptor shadows totally, so both names have no source but these rows. fsctl: SDK unistd.h:785 `int fsctl(const char *, unsigned long, void *, unsigned int)` — the path-based fs-control sibling of ioctl that sqlite AFP locking issues at os_unix.c:3013 `err = fsctl(path, afpfsByteRangeLock2FSCTL, &pb, 0)` (the request VALUE side of that call lives in sys/ioctl.json's _IOWR macho arm — the two descriptors meet at exactly this site); libSystem-only export (link-verified; no glibc/msvcrt fsctl exists) → per-symbol [macho]. uuid_t: `typedef unsigned char __darwin_uuid_t[16]` → uuid_t (SDK sys/_types.h:89 + sys/_types/_uuid_t.h:31) — a 16-byte u8 ARRAY, this file's FIRST `typedefs` surface. Typedefs carry NO per-entry availableObjectFormats (a closed key set in shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp) — per-entry availability IS which `variants` exist (the sys/types.json fixpt_t/segsz_t mechanism): the single macho arm matches nothing on elf/pe → not injected → an elf/pe reference stays an honest S0006. Consumers, all inside `#if defined(__APPLE__) && SQLITE_ENABLE_LOCKING_STYLE`: os_unix.c:7600 `extern int gethostuuid(uuid_t id, …)`, :7607 `assert(PROXY_HOSTIDLEN == sizeof(uuid_t))`, :7791 `uuid_t myHostID` — sizeof MUST be 16 (PROXY_HOSTIDLEN) or the proxy conch layout shears. Pinned by tests/ffi RealUnistdJsonFsctlMachoOnly + RealUnistdJsonUuidTMachoOnlyTypedef and the shipped_bsd_random_futimes_uuid_macho corpus, whose exit arithmetic IS sizeof(uuid_t). ★ D-LK-SQLITE-MACHO-UNDEFINED-LIBSYSTEM-SYMBOLS: flock + statfs/fstatfs + sysctl/sysctlbyname — five more Darwin-only libSystem externs sqlite's DEFAULT macho path references (NOT opt-in like the AFP cluster above), each K_SymbolUndefined at link until declared, because DSS imports only DECLARED shipped externs. Consumers: os_unix.c (flock, statfs, fstatfs), mem1.c (sysctlbyname), test1.c (sysctl). PLACEMENT is organizational, not functional — the consuming oracle is a global scan of symbols[].name across ALL descriptors, so it does not matter which file a row lives in; they join fsctl HERE (rather than in new sys/file.json + sys/mount.json + sys/sysctl.json descriptors) because a descriptor SHADOWS the real SDK header TOTALLY (src/core/types/include_path_resolve.hpp:75-79), so a new partial descriptor would REGRESS the D-INCLUDE-ANGLE-SOURCE-FALLBACK that currently makes these TUs compile — the exact reason fsctl, a <sys/mount.h> name, already lives in this file. Signatures MEASURED against the real SDK (xcrun --show-sdk-path), each compile-verified by assigning the SDK symbol to a function pointer of the declared shape under `-Werror -Wincompatible-pointer-types`: flock = sys/fcntl.h:616 `int flock(int, int)` — NOTE it is NOT in sys/file.h, whose __BEGIN_DECLS block is EMPTY and which merely re-includes sys/fcntl.h; statfs = sys/mount.h:460 `int statfs(const char *, struct statfs *)`; fstatfs = sys/mount.h:442 `int fstatfs(int, struct statfs *)`; sysctl = sys/sysctl.h:800 `int sysctl(int *, u_int, void *, size_t *, void *, size_t)`; sysctlbyname = sys/sysctl.h:802 `int sysctlbyname(const char *, void *, size_t *, void *, size_t)`. `struct statfs *` becomes ptr<void> (the fsctl/futimes opaque-pointer convention — no consumer here needs its layout); size_t* becomes ptr<u64> and u_int becomes u32 (sys/_types/_u_int.h:30 `typedef unsigned int u_int`, _Static_assert-verified 4 bytes unsigned). All five carry FLAT signatures with NO signatureByDataModel, and that flatness is CORRECT rather than lazy: each row is [macho]-gated and all EIGHT macho64-* formats declare dataModel LP64, so no other data model can ever select them (the random/strtoll availability-narrowed rationale). ★★ TF-C121 (D-FFI-SHIPPED-SYMBOL-PER-TARGET-LINK-NAME) — statfs/fstatfs now carry the per-arch link name, and the CAVEAT that used to stand here CLOSED WITH A FALSE REASSURANCE that must be recorded, not quietly deleted. It said: 'on an x86_64-macho host the SDK asm label makes the call site reference `_statfs$INODE64` while this row imports `_statfs`, i.e. the leg stays LOUD (K_SymbolUndefined) rather than silently misbinding.' ⛔ MEASURED FALSE, and wrong in the dangerous direction. A DESCRIPTOR SHADOWS THE SDK HEADER TOTALLY — src/core/types/include_path_resolve.hpp states the `#include <h>` precedence as '1. Descriptor … 2. Source — NO descriptor, but a REAL source header on the -I includeDirs', so once unistd.json exists the SDK's `__DARWIN_INODE64` asm label NEVER PARTICIPATES in the build at all. There is no call site left to reference `_statfs$INODE64`: DSS declares the plain name, DSS imports the plain name, libSystem's x86_64 slice EXPORTS the plain name (the legacy 32-bit-ino_t implementation), so the program links clean, loads clean, and misbinds SILENTLY. The whole 'the header disagrees with us so the linker will catch it' reasoning presumed a header we had already replaced. The same wrong inference sat in sys/stat.json and dirent.json; all three are corrected. ★ The measurement is unchanged and still holds (sys/cdefs.h `__DARWIN_ONLY_64_BIT_INO_T` = 0 on x86_64 / 1 on arm64; matched two-arch control on macOS 26.5.2 emits `_statfs$INODE64`/`_fstatfs$INODE64` vs `_statfs`/`_fstatfs`) — only the CONSEQUENCE was misjudged. The fix is the exact structural analogue of what `version` did for elf, as predicted: `linkName` declares the UNDECORATED base per (arch, format) and the ENGINE composes Mach-O's leading `_`. ★ AND THE AUTHORING CHECKLIST MISSED IT TOO: 'verify the symbol is exported' passes here, because BOTH spellings are exported by libsystem_kernel.tbd. The check that works is 'does a real compiler for THIS target emit THIS name for THIS C identifier'. ★ LANE-F: `environ` — the POSIX-BLESSED environment interface, and it lands HERE because line 566 of glibc's own /usr/include/unistd.h is where `extern char **environ;` lives (POSIX.1 does not specify main's third parameter at all, so `environ` — not `envp` — is what portable code uses). ★★ IT SHIPS AS THE MACRO/SYMBOL SPLIT `environ` -> `__environ`, NOT AS AN `environ` DATA ROW, AND THE FIRST CUT OF THIS ROW *DID* SHIP THE OBVIOUS SHAPE AND WAS SILENTLY WRONG — recorded because the failure mode is the TF-C121 `_realpath$DARWIN_EXTSN` class exactly: a name that LINKS CLEAN, LOADS CLEAN, and binds the wrong thing. An `environ` row with `kind: object` produced a correct-looking binary — `readelf -r` showed `R_X86_64_COPY … environ + 0` and the dynsym showed `environ` as an 8-byte OBJECT — and it READ NULL AT RUNTIME on all four legs (x86_64/arm64 × debug/release, rc=1 from the witness's first guard). ✔ROOT-CAUSED BY A MATCHED gcc CONTROL rather than by theory: the same program built `gcc -std=gnu17 -no-pie` RUNS (rc=42) and its copy relocation is against **`__environ@GLIBC_2.2.5`** — the STRONG alias — while its dynsym defines BOTH `__environ` (GLOBAL) and `environ` (WEAK) at ONE exec address. That is the whole mechanism: glibc's own startup writes the environment pointer through its INTERNAL name `__environ`, and a copy relocation only redirects libc's references for the symbol the exec actually claims. Claim the weak `environ` alone and libc keeps writing its OWN .bss slot while the exec reads a copy that ld.so filled from that slot BEFORE `__libc_start_main` ran — i.e. 0. Claim `__environ` and libc's write lands in the exec's slot, which is what gcc does and why gcc's binary works. So the SYMBOL is `__environ` (`kind: object`, typed `ptr<ptr<char>>` — the `char **` spelling strtoll's endptr already uses — bound through the ELF exec formats' declared `dataImportBinding: copy-relocation`) and `environ` is an elf-gated MACRO onto it: the stdio.json macho `stdin`->`__stdinp` shape verbatim, pure config, no engine change. ⓘ THIS ALSO MIRRORS THE REAL HEADER: glibc's /usr/include/unistd.h declares `extern char **__environ;` UNCONDITIONALLY and `extern char **environ;` only under `#ifdef __USE_GNU`, so `__environ` is the always-present spelling and `environ` the convenience alias — measured, and the reason a plain `gcc -std=c17`/`-std=gnu17` compile of `environ` FAILS `'environ' undeclared` without `_GNU_SOURCE` (which is why the cross-check reference for the corpus witness is `-std=gnu17 -D_GNU_SOURCE`, not the `-std=c17` this clause first claimed). EAGER-IMPORT SAFE ([[D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT]]), MEASURED BEFORE SHIPPING on BOTH elf run legs and on two concurring instruments: `nm -D` reports `V environ@@GLIBC_2.2.5` at 0x20ad58 (x86_64, /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6) and `V environ@@GLIBC_2.17` at 0x1b7288 (aarch64, /usr/aarch64-linux-gnu/lib/libc.so.6), and `objdump -T` concurs on both with `w DO .bss` SIZE 8 — a WEAK DATA OBJECT, and weak-is-safe (present ⇒ resolvable at load; only ABSENT breaks). glibc aliases `environ`/`_environ`/`__environ` to the SAME address on both arches (`__environ` is the strong `B`/`g` one), so the un-prefixed POSIX spelling is a real export, not a header artifact. ⚠ THE `@@GLIBC_x.y` SUFFIX MEANS A GREP ANCHORED ON `$` RETURNS A FALSE ABSENT — the stdio.json popen/pclose warning, and the reason the matcher here is ` (environ|_environ|__environ)(@|$)`. ★ ELF-ONLY, and BOTH exclusions are deliberate rather than unfinished. macho is DEFERRED under this directory's need-driven staging rule (the fileno/popen-pclose precedent: a symbol ships when a consumer lands AND its export is MEASURED, never on inference) — there is no macho consumer, and the export could not be measured this cycle without waking the operator's Mac; an inferred macho row would risk EVERY macho binary's LOAD, which is the whole reason that rule exists. pe is a DIFFERENT and more interesting exclusion: ✔MEASURED, NEITHER Windows CRT EXPORTS `environ` AT ALL — `objdump -p` plus a direct PE export-directory parse over ucrtbase.dll (2,484 exports) and msvcrt.dll (1,330) find no `environ`, no `_environ`, no `__environ` in ucrtbase, and only the UNDERSCORED `_environ` (msvcrt DATA export, ordinal 270) in the legacy image. So the claim 'both platforms export it' holds only for the underscored Windows spelling, and a pe `environ` would have to be a MACRO onto UCRT's `__p__environ` ACCESSOR (ordinal 87, returning `char***` — ucrtbase exposes NO data export for it, permanently, exactly as `_fmode` goes through `_get_fmode`/`__p__fmode`). That macro is expressible in TODAY's vocabulary (it is the `stdin`->`(__acrt_iob_func(0))` shape verbatim, needing no engine change). ⓘ THE PLACEMENT FORK THIS CLAUSE POSED IS NOW RESOLVED, AND THE HALF IT RULED OUT IS THE HALF THAT HAPPENED: it said the macro 'CANNOT LIVE IN THIS FILE — this descriptor is `availableObjectFormats: [elf, macho]`, i.e. there is no `<unistd.h>` on pe at all', and named the alternative (a POSIX name in `<stdlib.h>` that neither glibc nor MSVC declares there) as the only other option. `<unistd.h>` IS on pe now (see the pe paragraph below), so this file is the correct home should a consumer ever appear — but `environ` itself is UNCHANGED and stays elf-only: the measurement that put it there (no Windows CRT exports ANY `environ` spelling) is untouched by the header becoming available, and this directory ships on a CONSUMER, of which there is still none. WITNESS: examples/c-subset/shipped_environ (elf x86_64 + arm64, with a `release` arm) + tests/ffi RealUnistdJsonEnvironElfOnlyDataObject. ★★★ LANE-CFG: `<unistd.h>` OPENS ON pe, MODELLED ON WHAT THE REFERENCE HEADER ACTUALLY IS — A THIN RE-EXPORT. ✔MEASURED against the same-platform oracle `C:/Strawberry/c/bin/x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc` (`-dumpmachine` = x86_64-w64-mingw32), whose `<unistd.h>` #includes <io.h>, <process.h>, <getopt.h> and then declares ONLY sleep/usleep/ftruncate/ftruncate64/truncate/truncate64/swab/getpid itself plus SEEK_* and STD{IN,OUT,ERR}_FILENO. Per-header probe (one TU each, `void *p = (void*)&NAME;`, rc read directly): <io.h> alone yields close read write lseek unlink rmdir access getcwd chdir isatty dup dup2; <process.h> alone yields getpid; <getopt.h> yields none of them. So the pe surface here is TWO gated `includes` edges (io.h, process.h) plus this file's own CONSTANTS — and NOT ONE symbol row is added on pe, which is why there is no `library.pe` key: on pe this descriptor imports nothing. Every previously-FLAT symbol row therefore carries an explicit `availableObjectFormats:[elf,macho]`; without it the header opening on pe would have declared 26 POSIX externs against a runtime that exports NONE of them, breaking every pe binary's LOAD at 0xC0000139 ([[D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT]]). ★ THE NAMES THE EDGES CARRY ARE DECLARED WHERE MINGW DECLARES THEM (io.json / process.json), as real FUNCTIONS with a per-format `linkName` onto the underscored ucrtbase export — NOT as macros: mingw declares `int write(int,const void*,unsigned)` and links it to `_write` through oldnames, and a `#define write _write` would additionally rewrite every struct member and local of that name. ★ DELIBERATELY ABSENT ON pe, each with its reason: getopt/optarg/optind/opterr/optopt — there is NO getopt.json in the corpus and an `includes` edge to a descriptor that does not exist is refused (invariant: EDGE FIRES ⇒ CHILD AVAILABLE); sleep/usleep — ucrtbase exports NEITHER, and the `_sleep` it DOES export takes MILLISECONDS where POSIX `sleep` takes SECONDS, so a linkName onto it would be a silent 1000x error of exactly the class this project refuses (the honest realization is a shipped-source body over kernel32 `Sleep`, and no consumer asks for one); ftruncate/ftruncate64/truncate/truncate64 — mingw realizes ftruncate as a header INLINE over `_chsize`, so no export named ftruncate exists to bind and the authoring check ('does a real compiler for THIS target emit THIS name for THIS C identifier') fails for a `_chsize` linkName; swab — `_swab` is a real ucrtbase export and the ABI matches byte for byte, but DSS declares `swab` on NO format today, so a pe-only arm would be the only place it exists. ★ THE CONSTANTS BELOW ARE FLAT AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: mingw's <io.h> defines F_OK 0 / X_OK 1 / W_OK 2 / R_OK 4 — byte-identical to the xnu/glibc values already recorded above — and SEEK_SET/CUR/END 0/1/2 come from mingw's <unistd.h> itself. STD{IN,OUT,ERR}_FILENO 0/1/2 are NEW and close a gap on EVERY format, not just pe: glibc /usr/include/unistd.h:210-212 and mingw <unistd.h>:22-25 both define them and DSS declared them nowhere. ★★ THE NON-SYMBOL SURFACES WERE CENSUSED TOO, AND THE ANSWER IS 'ALREADY GATED' — RECORDED WITH ITS MEASUREMENT SO IT IS NOT RE-LITIGATED. Opening a header on a new format is a per-ROW question on EVERY surface kind, not just `symbols`, and the four non-symbol rows here that mingw does NOT provide (`environ` macro, `uuid_t` typedef, `_SC_PAGESIZE` and `_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN` constants — each probed against the oracle with a `#include <unistd.h>` TU) needed no edit, because for `macros`/`typedefs`/`constants` PER-ENTRY AVAILABILITY *IS* WHICH `variants` EXIST (the sys/types.json fixpt_t/segsz_t mechanism, already stated above) and all four are variants-only with no pe arm. ✔MEASURED THROUGH THE COMPILER, not read off the JSON, and with a DISCRIMINATING control so the result cannot be vacuous: one TU per name, `--target` the only difference — `environ`, `_SC_PAGESIZE`, `_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN` are RESOLVED on elf64 and FAIL LOUD on pe64; `uuid_t` fails loud on both (its only arm is macho); and the seven rows that MUST survive on pe (`SEEK_SET/CUR/END`, `F_OK/X_OK/W_OK/R_OK`, `STD{IN,OUT,ERR}_FILENO`) RESOLVE on both. A gate that never fires and a gate that fires on everything look identical without that second half. ★ THE GENERAL RULE THE `_SC_*` PAIR ILLUSTRATES: AN ARGUMENT CONSTANT TRAVELS WITH ITS FUNCTION. `_SC_PAGESIZE` and `_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN` exist only to be passed to `sysconf`, and `sysconf` is `[elf,macho]` — so a pe arm on either constant would publish a value whose ONLY consumer is a name that fails loud on that target, i.e. a surface that can be spelled and can never be used. Whenever a constant's meaning is 'the argument selecting a behaviour of F', its availability set must be a SUBSET of F's; the two are one fact and drifting them apart produces a header that lies in the quiet direction. ★★★ OPERATOR RULING ("if we need to build some of our own headers, SO BE IT. DO IT. NO WORKAROUNDS"): the names mingw's <unistd.h> declares ITSELF now SHIP ON pe AS A REALIZED BODY, `runtime/platform/src/unistd.c` (the dirent.c precedent; `realization.pe` is the binding fact and there is deliberately no `library.pe`, since one format naming both an image and a source is refusal R3). 'No consumer asks for it' was REJECTED as a reason to omit a name the reference declares — the bar is bidirectional. THE SEVEN: sleep, usleep, ftruncate, ftruncate64, truncate, truncate64, swab. ★★ EACH IS A BODY RATHER THAN A `linkName` FOR A MEASURED REASON, AND THE FIRST IS A TRAP: ucrtbase DOES export `_sleep`, and it takes MILLISECONDS where POSIX `sleep` takes SECONDS, so binding it would link clean, load clean and sleep 1/1000th of the request — `objdump -p` over 4340 name-table entries finds `_sleep` and finds NO `sleep`/`usleep` at all. `ftruncate` is a HEADER INLINE over `_chsize` on mingw, so no symbol of that name exists to bind and the linkName authoring check fails by construction. ⓘ WIDTHS: `off32_t` is `long`, which LLP64 makes 32-bit, so the un-suffixed pair carries an i32 offset and the `64` pair i64 — collapsing them would silently truncate every offset above 2 GiB, which is the whole reason both spellings exist. ★ `swab` ALSO LANDS ON elf/macho, because glibc declares it (/usr/include/unistd.h:1171 `void swab(const void*, void*, ssize_t)`, exported `T swab@@GLIBC_2.2.5` — STRONG, eager-import safe) and DSS declared it on no format: the pe row carries mingw's `(char*,char*,int)` shape and the POSIX row glibc's, hence two rows rather than one. ★★ RED-ON-DISABLE, RUN AGAINST THE REAL BODY AND REPORTED PER MUTANT: sleep-as-milliseconds -> exit 4 with the witness's WALL TIME collapsing 1306ms -> 289ms (the exact `_sleep` signature); swab-without-swapping -> exit 16384; ftruncate-returns-0-without-resizing -> exit 256. Each mutant differed by md5, still parsed, reddened ONLY its own bit, and the RESTORED column returned to exit 0 at 1293ms. ★ F_OK/X_OK/W_OK/R_OK MOVED TO PER-FORMAT arms here (elf+macho) because mingw defines them in <io.h>:182-185, not in <unistd.h> — on pe they now arrive over the io.h edge, which is both reference-true AND why no duplicate name enters the pe closure.
